metadata.subject: Rust programming language
metadata.language_version: Version-aware overview; verify edition- and compiler-specific details before treating them as normative

source_policy.source_attribution: Primary input: user-provided Rust programming language article excerpt. Descriptions are normalized into graph entities; some connections are structured explanatory modeling rather than verbatim source claims.
notes: This is a knowledge-graph instance plus a JSON Schema contract, not the Rust compiler's formal grammar or an official language specification.
Rust features, tool behavior, editions, and APIs may vary by compiler version and target.
Validate every relationship endpoint against entities[].id before graph ingestion.

entities.name: Rust
entities.description: General-purpose, multi-paradigm systems programming language emphasizing performance, type safety, concurrency, and memory safety without a conventional garbage collector.

entities.name: Performance
entities.description: Rust targets low-level control and efficient compiled code, including zero-cost abstractions and opportunities for zero-copy processing.

entities.name: Type safety
entities.description: Static type checking rejects incompatible operations and invalid type use before program execution.

entities.name: Memory safety
entities.description: Safe Rust's type and ownership rules prevent common invalid-memory operations, subject to the limits of unsafe code and external interfaces.

entities.name: Data-race freedom
entities.description: Safe Rust's concurrency and aliasing rules prevent data races for properly modeled shared state.

entities.name: Multi-paradigm programming
entities.description: Rust combines imperative and structured programming with functional concepts, generic programming, and concurrency.

entities.name: Zero-cost abstractions
entities.description: Many abstractions compile away or specialize at compile time, avoiding inherent runtime costs where possible.

entities.name: fn keyword
entities.description: Declares a function; function signatures express parameters and return types.

entities.name: let binding
entities.description: Introduces a local binding; bindings are immutable unless mut is specified.

entities.name: mut modifier
entities.description: Permits mutation of a binding or mutable access where the type and borrowing rules allow it.

entities.name: Variable shadowing
entities.description: A new let binding may reuse a name, including with a different type, without mutating the previous binding.

entities.name: Block expression
entities.description: A brace-delimited block evaluates to its final expression when that expression lacks a trailing semicolon.

entities.name: if expression
entities.description: Branches on a boolean condition and can itself yield a value when branches have compatible types.

entities.name: match expression
entities.description: Performs exhaustive pattern matching over values and enum variants.

entities.name: if let
entities.description: Matches a single pattern conveniently, optionally with an else branch.

entities.name: loop expression
entities.description: Repeats indefinitely until exited, and can return a value through break.

entities.name: while loop
entities.description: Repeats while a boolean condition evaluates to true.

entities.name: for loop
entities.description: Iterates over values produced by an IntoIterator/iterator expression.

entities.name: break
entities.description: Exits a loop; loop expressions can return the break value.

entities.name: continue
entities.description: Skips to the next iteration of the innermost or labeled loop.

entities.name: return expression
entities.description: Returns from the current function, optionally carrying a value.

entities.name: Semicolon
entities.description: Terminates statements and suppresses the value of an expression in statement position.

entities.name: Pattern matching
entities.description: Destructures and tests values using patterns in match, if let, let, and related constructs.

entities.name: Closures
entities.description: Anonymous function-like values that can capture their environment by borrow, mutable borrow, or move.

entities.name: Iterator trait
entities.description: Defines sequential value production through next and supports adapter/consumer chains.

entities.name: Iterator adapters
entities.description: Methods such as map and filter transform iterator pipelines, often lazily.

entities.name: Range expressions
entities.description: Expressions such as 1..5 and 1..=5 create range values, commonly used with iterators.

entities.name: Macros
entities.description: Compile-time code generation mechanisms that expand into Rust syntax or items.

entities.name: macro_rules!
entities.description: Declarative macro mechanism that matches token patterns and expands templates.

entities.name: Procedural macros
entities.description: Compiler-invoked Rust functions that transform token streams; include derive, attribute, and function-like forms.

entities.name: Attributes
entities.description: Metadata syntax such as #[derive(...)] and #![no_std] that affects compilation or tooling.

entities.name: unsafe
entities.description: Marks operations or blocks where the programmer must uphold additional safety obligations.

entities.name: Unit type ()
entities.description: The single-valued type used when no meaningful value is returned; ordinary functions without an explicit return type return unit.

entities.name: bool
entities.description: Boolean type with values true and false.

entities.name: char
entities.description: A 32-bit Unicode scalar value, excluding surrogate code points.

entities.name: i8
entities.description: 8-bit signed integer type.

entities.name: i16
entities.description: 16-bit signed integer type.

entities.name: i32
entities.description: 32-bit signed integer type and default integer type absent other inference.

entities.name: i64
entities.description: 64-bit signed integer type.

entities.name: i128
entities.description: 128-bit signed integer type.

entities.name: u8
entities.description: 8-bit unsigned integer type; also used for byte-oriented data.

entities.name: u16
entities.description: 16-bit unsigned integer type.

entities.name: u32
entities.description: 32-bit unsigned integer type.

entities.name: u64
entities.description: 64-bit unsigned integer type.

entities.name: u128
entities.description: 128-bit unsigned integer type.

entities.name: isize
entities.description: Signed integer type sized to the target pointer width.

entities.name: usize
entities.description: Unsigned integer type sized to the target pointer width; commonly used for indexing and sizes.

entities.name: f32
entities.description: IEEE 754 single-precision floating-point type.

entities.name: f64
entities.description: IEEE 754 double-precision floating-point type and default float type absent other inference.

entities.name: Tuple
entities.description: Fixed-length compound value whose fields may have different types; tuple fields are accessed by numeric position.

entities.name: Array
entities.description: Fixed-length collection of values all having the same element type, represented as [T; N].

entities.name: Slice
entities.description: Dynamically sized view of a contiguous sequence, typically borrowed as &[T] or &mut [T].

entities.name: str
entities.description: Dynamically sized UTF-8 string slice type, normally accessed through references such as &str.

entities.name: String
entities.description: Owned, growable UTF-8 string type from the standard library.

entities.name: struct
entities.description: Declares a named record-like type with fields; layout is not generally a stable ABI unless explicitly represented.

entities.name: enum
entities.description: Declares a type with one of several variants; variants can carry associated data.

entities.name: type alias
entities.description: Gives another name to an existing type without creating a distinct nominal type.

entities.name: Generics
entities.description: Parameterized functions, types, traits, and implementations whose parameters are constrained by bounds.

entities.name: Option<T>
entities.description: Represents an optional value with Some(T) or None, making absence explicit in the type.

entities.name: Result<T, E>
entities.description: Represents success as Ok(T) or failure as Err(E), supporting explicit error propagation.

entities.name: &T
entities.description: Shared immutable borrow; safe references are non-null, aligned, and valid for their inferred lifetime.

entities.name: &mut T
entities.description: Exclusive mutable borrow; borrowing rules prevent conflicting active accesses.

entities.name: *const T
entities.description: Raw const pointer that may be null, dangling, or misaligned; dereferencing requires unsafe.

entities.name: *mut T
entities.description: Raw mutable pointer that may be null, dangling, or misaligned; dereferencing requires unsafe.

entities.name: Box<T>
entities.description: Owning smart pointer for heap allocation with unique ownership by default.

entities.name: Rc<T>
entities.description: Single-threaded reference-counted shared ownership pointer; not thread-safe for cross-thread sharing.

entities.name: Arc<T>
entities.description: Atomically reference-counted shared ownership pointer for sharing ownership across threads when T satisfies required bounds.

entities.name: Cell<T>
entities.description: Interior-mutability container permitting value replacement through shared references when its rules are met.

entities.name: RefCell<T>
entities.description: Interior-mutability container enforcing borrow rules at runtime.

entities.name: Mutex<T>
entities.description: Synchronization primitive that grants exclusive access through a lock guard.

entities.name: RwLock<T>
entities.description: Synchronization primitive allowing multiple readers or one writer, subject to lock behavior.

entities.name: Pin
entities.description: Pointer wrapper used to constrain movement of a pointee when required by pinning APIs and invariants.

entities.name: PhantomData<T>
entities.description: Zero-sized marker used to express ownership, variance, or drop-check relationships to the compiler.

entities.name: Ownership
entities.description: Each value has one owner at a time; ownership can move between bindings and function calls.

entities.name: Move semantics
entities.description: A non-Copy value passed or assigned by value is typically moved, invalidating the previous binding for further use.

entities.name: Copy trait
entities.description: Types implementing Copy are copied by value rather than moved in ordinary copy contexts; Copy is limited to types whose duplication is bitwise/simple and does not require custom destruction.

entities.name: Borrowing
entities.description: A reference temporarily accesses a value without transferring ownership.

entities.name: Shared borrowing
entities.description: Multiple immutable borrows may coexist when no conflicting mutable borrow is active.

entities.name: Mutable borrowing
entities.description: A mutable borrow provides exclusive access for its active lifetime, preventing conflicting accesses.

entities.name: Borrow checker
entities.description: Compiler analysis enforces ownership, reference validity, and aliasing rules.

entities.name: Lifetime
entities.description: A lifetime describes the region in which a reference is valid; most lifetimes are inferred.

entities.name: Named lifetime parameter
entities.description: Syntax such as 'a relates reference validity across signatures and types.

entities.name: Lifetime elision
entities.description: Rules allow many function signatures to omit explicit lifetime parameters when relationships can be inferred.

entities.name: Non-lexical lifetimes
entities.description: Borrow checking can end a borrow after its last relevant use rather than only at the end of the enclosing lexical scope.

entities.name: Drop and destruction
entities.description: A value is dropped when it leaves scope or is otherwise destroyed; Drop can define cleanup behavior.

entities.name: RAII
entities.description: Resource acquisition and release are tied to value lifetime, commonly through ownership and Drop.

entities.name: Interior mutability
entities.description: Abstractions such as Cell and RefCell permit mutation through shared references while enforcing their respective rules.

entities.name: Unsafe Rust
entities.description: A subset that enables operations requiring programmer-maintained invariants; unsafe does not disable all compiler checks.

entities.name: Undefined behavior
entities.description: Invalid operations, often in unsafe code or violated foreign contracts, for which Rust does not guarantee program behavior.

entities.name: Trait
entities.description: Declares shared behavior through required methods, associated types/constants, and optional default implementations.

entities.name: impl block
entities.description: Defines inherent methods for a type or implements a trait for a type.

entities.name: Trait bound
entities.description: Constrains generic types to implement required traits, for example T: Display.

entities.name: where clause
entities.description: Expresses trait and lifetime constraints in a separate clause for complex signatures.

entities.name: Static dispatch
entities.description: Generic calls are usually monomorphized for concrete types at compile time.

entities.name: Dynamic dispatch
entities.description: Trait objects such as dyn Trait invoke methods through a runtime vtable.

entities.name: Trait object
entities.description: Type-erased value paired with trait method metadata, commonly used behind references or smart pointers.

entities.name: Associated type
entities.description: Trait-declared type selected by an implementation.

entities.name: derive macros
entities.description: Attributes such as #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)] generate common trait implementations.

entities.name: Display trait
entities.description: Formatting trait for user-facing textual representation.

entities.name: Debug trait
entities.description: Formatting trait for programmer-oriented diagnostic output.

entities.name: Send trait
entities.description: Marker trait indicating a type can be transferred safely between threads under Rust's rules.

entities.name: Sync trait
entities.description: Marker trait indicating references to a type can be shared safely between threads under Rust's rules.

entities.name: Iterator
entities.description: Protocol for producing a sequence of values through next.

entities.name: IntoIterator
entities.description: Conversion protocol that produces an iterator, used by for loops and iterator APIs.

entities.name: collect
entities.description: Iterator consumer that builds a collection or other FromIterator target when the type is inferable.

entities.name: map
entities.description: Iterator adapter that transforms each item.

entities.name: filter
entities.description: Iterator adapter that keeps items satisfying a predicate.

entities.name: Closure capture
entities.description: Closures infer how to capture environment values, with move available to capture by value.

entities.name: Explicit error handling
entities.description: Rust commonly models recoverable errors using Result and absence using Option rather than exceptions.

entities.name: ? operator
entities.description: Propagates compatible residual error/absence from Result or Option contexts and returns early when propagation applies.

entities.name: panic!
entities.description: Signals an unrecoverable programming failure; unwinding or abort behavior depends on build configuration and target.

entities.name: unwrap
entities.description: Extracts a success/present value or panics if the value is an error/None.

entities.name: Vec<T>
entities.description: Growable contiguous owned vector from the standard library.

entities.name: HashMap<K,V>
entities.description: Hash-based key-value collection from the standard library.

entities.name: HashSet<T>
entities.description: Hash-based set collection from the standard library.

entities.name: BTreeMap<K,V>
entities.description: Ordered key-value map implemented using a B-tree.

entities.name: no_std
entities.description: Crate-level attribute that avoids the standard library; core remains available and alloc may be used when configured.

entities.name: core
entities.description: Fundamental library with language-level primitives and no OS-dependent facilities.

entities.name: alloc
entities.description: Allocation-backed collection and smart-pointer facilities usable without the full standard library when an allocator is supplied.

entities.name: std
entities.description: Standard library adding OS, I/O, threading, networking, and other platform facilities.

entities.name: Module system
entities.description: Organizes items and controls visibility with mod, pub, paths, and use.

entities.name: Crate
entities.description: Rust compilation unit/package target; a crate is a library or binary root.

entities.name: Cargo workspace
entities.description: Groups related packages and shares build coordination and commonly a lockfile.

entities.name: Cargo.toml
entities.description: Manifest declaring package metadata, targets, features, dependencies, and build configuration.

entities.name: Cargo.lock
entities.description: Records exact resolved dependency versions for reproducible application builds; library policy may vary.

entities.name: crates.io
entities.description: Public package registry commonly used by Cargo.

entities.name: rustup
entities.description: Toolchain installer and manager for Rust compiler versions, components, and targets.

entities.name: rustc
entities.description: Rust compiler that parses, analyzes, lowers, optimizes, and emits compiled artifacts.

entities.name: Cargo
entities.description: Rust build system and package manager; also integrates common development commands.

entities.name: rustfmt
entities.description: Code formatter that applies configured Rust formatting conventions.

entities.name: Clippy
entities.description: Linting tool that detects suspicious patterns and suggests correctness, performance, and style improvements.

entities.name: rust-analyzer
entities.description: Language Server Protocol implementation providing IDE features such as completion, navigation, and diagnostics.

entities.name: Abstract syntax tree
entities.description: Structured representation of parsed source syntax.

entities.name: Intermediate representations
entities.description: Compiler representations used between source parsing and backend code generation.

entities.name: LLVM backend
entities.description: Default major code-generation backend for rustc on many targets.

entities.name: GCC Rust front end
entities.description: Alternative Rust compiler front end in the GCC project; support and compatibility depend on version.

entities.name: Cranelift backend
entities.description: Alternative code-generation backend used in some Rust toolchain workflows.

entities.name: Linker
entities.description: Combines object files and libraries into a final executable or shared artifact.

entities.name: Rust edition
entities.description: Edition system permits selected language evolution while maintaining interoperability among crates using different editions.

entities.name: Stable channel
entities.description: Release channel intended for stable, supported language and toolchain features.

entities.name: Beta channel
entities.description: Pre-release channel used to test the next stable Rust release.

entities.name: Nightly channel
entities.description: Frequently updated channel where experimental features may be available behind feature gates.

entities.name: Foreign function interface
entities.description: Mechanisms for calling external-language functions and exposing Rust functions to other languages.

entities.name: extern C
entities.description: Declares functions or blocks using the C ABI for interoperability.

entities.name: repr(C)
entities.description: Representation attribute for C-compatible layout expectations where the type's field types and ABI are compatible.

entities.name: bindgen
entities.description: Tool that can generate Rust FFI bindings from C/C++ headers.

entities.name: cxx crate
entities.description: Ecosystem tool for defining and generating safer Rust/C++ interop bridges.

entities.name: async/await
entities.description: Syntax for asynchronous computations; async functions produce futures that are polled by an executor.

entities.name: Future trait
entities.description: Represents a value that may become available later through polling.

entities.name: Async executor
entities.description: Runtime component that schedules and polls futures.

entities.name: Tokio
entities.description: Popular asynchronous runtime ecosystem for networking, timers, and task scheduling.

entities.name: OS thread
entities.description: Standard-library thread abstraction for concurrent execution.

entities.name: Channel
entities.description: Message-passing abstraction for transferring values between concurrent tasks or threads.

entities.name: Atomic types
entities.description: Atomic operations enable synchronization on supported primitive values under defined memory orderings.

entities.name: MutexGuard
entities.description: RAII guard representing acquired mutex access; dropping the guard releases the lock.

entities.name: WebAssembly target
entities.description: Compilation target for portable sandboxed execution environments, subject to target and runtime support.

entities.name: Embedded Rust
entities.description: Rust use in constrained or bare-metal targets, often using no_std and target-specific HALs.

entities.name: Formal verification
entities.description: Methods and tools for proving properties of Rust programs or subsets of their semantics.

entities.name: Kani
entities.description: Bounded model checker for Rust code.

entities.name: Miri
entities.description: Interpreter used to detect certain classes of undefined behavior and invalid operations in Rust programs.

entities.name: Aeneas
entities.description: Research tool for translating or reasoning about Rust programs for verification.

entities.name: Creusot
entities.description: Deductive verification tool for Rust programs.

entities.name: Prusti
entities.description: Verification tool using specifications and verification conditions for Rust.

entities.name: Verus
entities.description: Verification system for Rust programs using a specification-oriented approach.

entities.name: Rust Foundation
entities.description: Nonprofit organization supporting Rust project infrastructure, trademarks, and ecosystem sustainability.

entities.name: Graydon Hoare
entities.description: Creator of Rust, who began it as a personal project in 2006.

entities.name: Mozilla
entities.description: Organization that sponsored Rust development beginning in 2009.

entities.name: Rust Team
entities.description: Project teams that maintain the language, compiler, libraries, tools, infrastructure, and community processes.

relationships.description: Rust is designed to support high-performance compiled software.
Rust's static type system contributes to type safety.
Rust's ownership and borrowing rules are central to safe memory access.
Safe concurrency relies on type and aliasing constraints.
Rust supports multiple programming paradigms.
The borrow checker enforces ownership and borrowing constraints.
A new let binding can reuse a name to shadow an earlier binding.
let bindings are immutable unless mut is specified.
A trailing semicolon suppresses an expression's value in statement position.
if conditions evaluate to bool.
match applies pattern matching to a value.
if let performs a convenient partial pattern match.
for loops consume values through iteration.
Standard range types implement iteration where applicable.
Adapters transform iterator pipelines.
map is an iterator adapter.
filter is an iterator adapter.
break exits a loop and may provide its result value.
Rust uses ownership to manage values and resources.
Ownership transfer commonly occurs through moves.
Borrowing provides access without transferring ownership.
Borrowing is represented through references.
Exclusive mutable borrowing is represented through &mut T.
Shared borrows are represented by shared references.
Mutable borrows are represented by mutable references.
Borrow checking validates reference validity across lifetimes.
Named lifetime parameters express relationships between reference validity regions.
Lifetime elision omits annotations where inference rules determine the relationships.
Non-lexical lifetimes improve precision of borrow-checking regions.
Drop and scope-based destruction support RAII resource management.
RAII relies on ownership and deterministic destruction.
unsafe marks blocks, functions, or operations with additional obligations.
Violating unsafe invariants can cause undefined behavior.
Dereferencing a raw pointer requires unsafe.
Dereferencing a raw pointer requires unsafe.
Option represents absence explicitly.
Result represents success or recoverable failure explicitly.
The ? operator propagates compatible Result errors.
The ? operator can propagate None in compatible Option contexts.
unwrap panics for Err or None.
panic is generally for unrecoverable failures rather than ordinary recoverable error propagation.
Generic parameters may be constrained by trait bounds.
where clauses express generic constraints.
An impl block may provide a trait implementation.
Trait objects normally use dynamic dispatch.
Generic calls commonly use monomorphization and static dispatch.
Trait objects provide runtime polymorphism.
Send bounds govern whether values may safely move between threads.
Sync bounds govern whether shared references may safely cross threads.
Arc enables shared ownership across threads when contained types meet thread-safety bounds.
Rc is not intended for cross-thread shared ownership.
Locking a Mutex produces a guard that releases the lock on drop.
Cell provides a form of interior mutability.
RefCell checks borrowing rules at runtime.
Vectors can be iterated over by reference or by value.
core is available in no_std programs.
alloc can be used in no_std contexts when allocation is configured.
std builds on core functionality.
std includes allocation-backed facilities.
Cargo reads Cargo.toml manifests.
Cargo uses Cargo.lock to preserve resolved dependency versions when present.
Cargo invokes rustc to compile package targets.
rustup installs and selects rustc toolchains.
rustfmt can be invoked through Cargo.
Clippy is commonly run through Cargo.
rust-analyzer uses project and compiler knowledge to provide IDE analysis.
rustc parses source into syntax structures such as an AST.
Source syntax is lowered through compiler intermediate representations.
The LLVM backend consumes compiler representations to generate machine code.
Backend output is linked into final artifacts.
A crate selects an edition that controls selected language interpretation rules.
Stable is a Rust compiler release channel.
Beta is a Rust compiler release channel.
Nightly is a Rust compiler release channel.
Rust FFI commonly declares C ABI boundaries with extern C.
repr(C) is commonly used for compatible struct or enum layout across FFI boundaries.
Calling foreign code and upholding foreign contracts may require unsafe blocks or unsafe declarations.
An async function produces a future.
A future normally needs an executor or caller to poll it to completion.
Tokio provides runtime and executor facilities.
Channels are commonly used to communicate between concurrent threads or tasks.
Atomics provide low-level synchronization across concurrent execution.
Rust can target WebAssembly when the selected target and dependencies support it.
Embedded targets commonly use no_std to reduce platform assumptions.
Miri can detect certain invalid operations and undefined-behavior patterns.
Kani is a bounded model checker used for Rust verification.
Aeneas supports research on translating/reasoning about Rust programs.
Creusot supports deductive verification of Rust programs.
Prusti supports specification-driven verification of Rust programs.
Verus supports formal verification of Rust programs.
Graydon Hoare began Rust as a personal project in 2006.
Mozilla officially sponsored Rust development beginning in 2009.
The Rust Foundation supports project infrastructure and ecosystem sustainability.
Rust project teams maintain the language and its ecosystem.
Cargo is the standard build and package-management tool for Rust projects.

taxonomy.id_conventions: Use lowercase snake_case IDs with stable semantic names. Relationship IDs use rel.NNNN. IDs should remain stable across enrichment; rename through explicit aliases or migration maps.
validation_rules: Every relationship source and target must match an entities[].id.
Use confidence=inferred for modeled relationships not explicitly asserted by a source.
Do not interpret unsafe as automatic undefined behavior; undefined behavior arises when required safety invariants are violated.
Do not treat all Rust references as runtime reference-counted pointers.
Mark compiler-version-specific, edition-specific, platform-specific, and nightly-only facts explicitly.
Keep source claims separate from explanatory inferences.
